title: dsoxlab meta.yml (contract v1)
description: Declarative contract of a lab-hosting repository, read by dsoxlab from <repo>/meta.yml. Contract version 1. Point your editor at this schema with a first line: # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stephrobert/dsoxlab/main/schemas/meta.schema.json

schema_version.description: Version of the INPUT contract this file follows. Leave it out and it is read as 1. Unrelated to the version of the JSON dsoxlab emits (reporting/machine.py: SCHEMA).

repo.description: Identity of the repository. The only block dsoxlab requires.

id.description: Slug of the repository. Namespaces the state directory and the service containers.

category.description: Technical category of the repository. Becomes the default section of every lab. Free-form: dsoxlab knows no list of domains. Optional since 0.1.88, because a repository that only provisions infrastructure has no lab to place; validate-structure asks for it as soon as labs exist.

blog_url.description: Home page of the online course.

issues_url.description: Where to file an issue about THIS catalogue rather than about the engine. Read by `dsoxlab support --issue`. Optional: without it the tool falls back to the repository's `origin` remote.

solutions.description: How this catalogue keeps its reference solutions. `encrypted` (the default) means every file under `solution/<lab path>` or `labs/<lab>/solution/` must be ansible-vault encrypted, and `validate-structure` reports any that is not: a solution shipped in clear text spoils the lab, and git keeps it forever. `plaintext` disarms that check, for a catalogue whose labs are chained, where one lab's starting point IS the previous lab's solution and the file therefore has to be copyable as a fixture. An unknown value falls back to `encrypted`: a check does not relax on a typo.

learning.description: Where this catalogue expects a proof of practice to be handed in. Optional, and a catalogue without it keeps working: dsoxlab then shows no link, invents no address and sends nothing. Nothing that looks like a secret belongs here, in either block: no token, API key, authorization header, webhook or command. A versioned repository is no place for a secret, and a catalogue gives the engine no orders.

portal_url.description: Hand-in URL, in https. It does NOT trigger any sending: it is a link the learner reads and decides to open, and `sync` below is what makes a push possible. It does not mean the portal is reachable from the machine running dsoxlab, nor that it is approved by anyone: it is declared by this catalogue, and the CLI says so. http is refused, except towards localhost with DSOXLAB_PORTAL_LOCAL set — a decision of the machine playing the lab, never of the catalogue.

sync.description: The synchronisation API this catalogue declares, so that `dsoxlab push` can hand proofs over without a browser. Optional, and absent by default: without it, `dsoxlab login` and `dsoxlab push` say this catalogue declares no synchronisation and nothing leaves the machine. Four public addresses and a PUBLIC OAuth client id, which PKCE allows to use with no secret: that is why this block can live in a versioned repository without exposing anything. A sending needs three things to coincide, and two are missing by default: this block, a `dsoxlab login`, and a `dsoxlab push` typed by the learner.

protocol.description: The synchronisation contract spoken by the portal. Only `learner-sync/1` is implemented. An unknown value makes the push refuse while naming what is expected: a payload emitted at random would be accepted by the gateway and then unreadable, and the learner would believe it synchronised.

api.description: Root of the API, in https. Paths come from the protocol, not from here.

issuer.description: The OIDC issuer, in https. It identifies the portal and names the local session file. Distinct from `oauth_domain`: with Cognito a custom domain serves the OAuth endpoints while the issuer stays the pool URL, and confusing the two yields a 404 on authorization.

oauth_domain.description: Root of the OAuth endpoints (/oauth2/authorize, /oauth2/token), in https.

client_id.description: Id of the PUBLIC OAuth client dedicated to the CLI. Not the site's own client: a web client only allows its own return URL. A second client is needed, declaring whichever return address callback_url or callback_port names.

callback_url.description: The https address where authorization returns, when no loopback is possible. The provider sends the learner there with the code in the URL, a page displays it, and the learner pastes it into the CLI. Sometimes the ONLY path: Cognito managed login version 2 refuses to serve an authorization whose return address is in http, loopback included, and answers 403 - measured on a real pool, same client, https 302 and http://127.0.0.1 403. Registering the address is therefore not enough, and the API accepts it without complaint. Mutually exclusive with callback_port.

callback_port.description: Port of the loopback address where authorization returns. FIXED, not ephemeral: the provider compares return URLs exactly, port included, so it must appear verbatim in the client configuration. Absent means not declared, and the connection says so rather than inventing one.

infra.description: Infrastructure topology. Optional, and needed only by labs declaring runtime: vm. A repository whose labs are all shell has no infra block at all.

provider.description: Infrastructure provider, or the list of candidates the learner may choose from. Providers packaged with dsoxlab: kvm, incus, outscale. Resolution order: DSOXLAB_PROVIDER, then the session context set by dsoxlab use --provider, then a bare string or a single-item list. Left unresolved is not an error: only infrastructure commands require one.

bootstrap.description: Playbook of the CATALOGUE's foundation, played once at the end of `provision`, before any lab. Path relative to the repository root. Optional: for a catalogue whose labs share an expensive base (a kubeadm cluster, a populated database, a directory), it replaces the include that every setup.yaml had to carry. It is played on the hosts of the generated inventory, so it targets `all` or `labenv`; it must be replayable without harm, and it is replayed when its content changes.

network.description: Name of the network the VMs join, dedicated to this repository so several catalogs can coexist.

cidr.description: Subnet of that network, in CIDR notation.

hosts.description: The VMs of the repository. Every runtime.targets[].host and every roles value of a lab must appear here by name.

name.description: FQDN of the machine, the name labs refer to.

distro.description: Image and cloud-init to use. Values packaged with dsoxlab today: alma10, alma9, ubuntu26, ubuntu24, ubuntu22, debian13, debian12. Not enumerated here, because the list lives in the Terraform templates and grows with them.

role.description: Free-form role, exposed as an Ansible host_var.

extra_disk_gb.description: Size of a second disk attached to the VM, for labs that need a real block device (partitioning, LVM, RAID). 0 = none.

ip.description: Legacy. Addresses come from the provider (Terraform output) and are injected into the generated inventory. Do not declare them.

providers.description: Per-provider overrides, read by the matching Terraform module. Keys are provider names; values are free-form mappings, because each provider has its own variables. The keys described below are the ones the packaged templates read; any other key is passed through untouched.

storage_pool.description: kvm only. libvirt storage pool the volumes are created in. Defaults to `default`, which a fresh install does not always declare: `virsh pool-list --all` is empty on a stock Ubuntu, and provisioning stops on a raw "Pool Not Found". Point this at a pool you own rather than editing the packaged template.

sections.description: Teaching order of the catalog. Optional. It orders and names the blocs; it never decides whether a lab exists, which is settled by the presence of labs/**/lab.yaml.

title.description: Human-readable name, shown as the bloc name.

labs.description: Paths relative to <repo>/labs/, in teaching order. The match is on the path, never on the lab id.
